audit.why: 50.08% over 1997 games is an even lane. Early is Orianna's (Malzahar has no pre-Voidling damage or escape), level 6 flips to Malzahar on Nether Grasp, and two-plus items returns to Orianna because Shockwave is a five-man ultimate against a single-target suppression. The full layer's phase sides were all 'Skill', contradicting the content layer and the packet chart.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides brought into line with the content layer and packet levelChart: Orianna 1/2/3, Skill 4-5, Malzahar 6, Skill first item, Orianna 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why described Orianna's level 6 as a doubling of her lane presence while the row is Malzahar's.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140/110/80 and is point-and-click suppression at 700 range. On the level 6 row the enemy owns the spike; the why must say so.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten to name the 140s rank-1 cooldown and the jungler collapse it enables.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nowhere on the page does it say that Void Shift grants crowd-control immunity, that Nether Grasp is an interruptible channel, or that Malefic Visions is a damage-over-time execute threat.
audit.why: Void Shift (P) gives 'massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity' that lingers briefly after he takes damage — a Shockwave cast into an intact Void Shift does not displace him. Nether Grasp (R) is flagged channel/'interruptible — any CC cancels it', so an allied stun frees the suppressed target. Malefic Visions (E, 11/10/9/8/7, 650 range) is flagged execute: it keeps ticking after you disengage and passes to a nearby unit on death, which also clears your caster minions and shoves the wave into you. Call of the Void (Q, 6s, 900 range) silences, denying your R and E casts.
audit.corrected: Chip Void Shift off with damage before you count on Shockwave landing; treat Nether Grasp as breakable by your team's CC; step in only after Call of the Void has fired; track the Visions tick as a health number, not a bar.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no cooldown number at all — packet defect confirms zero sequencing cues.
audit.why: The field exists to hold real numbers: R 140/110/80, Q 6s flat, E 11/10/9/8/7.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three real cooldowns and a 'step in after it fires' cue for the Q silence.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wave section was generic Orianna text with no Malzahar mechanic in it.
audit.why: Malefic Visions chaining through caster minions is his waveclear and it shoves the lane into you for free.
audit.corrected: breakdown.wave grounded in the Visions chain and in crashing on Nether Grasp's downtime.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d were unrelated strings pasted under their titles (copy-paste bleed).
audit.why: The title promises passive auto-weaving and Shockwave discipline; the bodies talked about his ultimate timing and about ball positioning.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles.

edits.before: Shockwave online — your lane presence doubles without casting anything. Every wave he contests is a potential flip.
edits.after: Nether Grasp is his row: point-click suppression on a 140s cooldown turns any jungler visit into a free kill. Hold Flash.

edits.before: - Malzahar Nether Grasp: matchup-defining — Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Check it before every step-up. - E Command: Protect is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Nether Grasp: 140s at rank 1, 110s at rank 2 — his one kill window, so step up on its downtime. - Call of the Void returns every 6s and its silence eats your R. - Malefic Visions: 11s at rank 1, 7s at rank 5 — fight when it is ticking on the wave, not on you.

edits.before: Malzahar wins by landing Nether Grasp, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Malzahar wins by saving Nether Grasp for a collapse and letting Malefic Visions tick you past your escape.

edits.before: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Void Shift makes him crowd-control immune, so chip it off before you count on Shockwave landing — a ball on his path forces that chip for free.

edits.before: Malzahar spends Nether Grasp early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Your passive ramps on repeat autos, and each hit keeps Void Shift from returning between casts.

edits.before: That is Malzahar’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: A ball parked out front cannot shield you when Visions ticks.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: R is 110s at rank 2 — spending it on minions leaves you no answer when he channels Nether Grasp onto your carry.

edits.before: Track Malzahar’s Nether Grasp: Point-and-click suppression — never step up solo while his passive shield is intact and R is up. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Nether Grasp is a channel — any hard CC on him breaks it, so your team's stun frees the suppressed target. Void Shift grants him CC immunity, so damage it off before you Shockwave.

edits.before: If Malzahar gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Nether Grasp extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q-W clears and stay relevant through Shockwave threat.
edits.after: If Malzahar gets a kill, his Malefic Visions economy snowballs — never dip under its tick damage and farm from max Q range instead. Two kills: clear voidlings with W and give his 700-range R that much room.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry by punishing a single-target ultimate: he spends Nether Grasp on one body, your Shockwave answers the other four — hold R until his has been used.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-W slow push you crash on roam timers — your clear is instant from Luden's and the ball travels with the shove. Worst wave: a frozen wave at his tower with the ball behind you — walking up ball-less into gank season is how Ori lanes end. Crash timing: shove with a destination in mind; mid waves are bus tickets, not chores.
edits.after: Best wave: crash before Malefic Visions starts chaining through your caster minions, because once it does he shoves you in for free. Worst wave: a frozen wave at his tower with the ball behind you — walking up ball-less into gank season is how Ori lanes end. Crash timing: shove on Nether Grasp's downtime, never while it is up and his jungler is unseen.

notes: Full layer and content layer disagreed on four level-chart rows (0,1,2,4): full said 'Skill' everywhere while content win[] and packet.levelChart said Orianna/Orianna/Orianna/.../Malzahar. Content was already correct and matches the whys, so only the full-layer sides are proposed; phases[4].why and rating are moved in the same group because the row's verdict changes hands. No content-layer chart edit is possible for these rows because the content side is already right. Not asserted anywhere: whether QSS/Cleanse removes Nether Grasp's suppression — the kit does not say and I did not verify it, so the page only states the kit-sourced fact that the channel breaks to CC on him. phases[N].rating left untouched: the rating scale is inconsistent across this dataset and I could not tell whether it encodes difficulty or advantage.
